articles.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas Tuchel
articles.summary: Real Madrid player must help improve defensive solidity. Scott, Hall, Lewis-Skelly and Calvert-Lewin selected. Thomas Tuchel has told Trent ­Alexander-Arnold he must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches.
body: The head coach has selected the Real Madrid right-back only once before – for the games against Andorra and Senegal in June last year. Tuchel made headlines when he did so by urging Alexander-Arnold to focus on the defensive side of his game or risk a slip that could undermine the team’s World Cup campaign.

Tuchel used him as a 64th-­minute substitute against Andorra and ­Alexander-Arnold was out of the ­picture by the time England went to North America for the tournament. He is now back, despite starting only three of Madrid’s seven matches this season and largely going under the radar with his performances. Tuchel’s message to him has not changed.
“He has to, it’s necessary,” Tuchel said when asked whether Alexander-Arnold offered enough defensively. “My conviction is that he will but he has no choice.”

Tuchel continues to see ­Alexander-Arnold, who is famed for the range of his passing, as a right-back rather than a midfielder. The head coach has previously said he has Tino ­Livramento and Jarell ­Quansah ahead of Alexander-Arnold in the right-back pecking order. He has named both of them in the squad for the games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and ­Croatia (away).

articles.title: Hedges pays tribute to late trainer Hatton at weigh-in
articles.summary: John Hedges pays tribute Ricky Hatton by wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with images of his late trainer as he weighs in for Saturday's fight with Pat Brown in Manchester.
body: Hatton, a two-weight world champion, was found dead at his Manchester home in September 2025, aged 46.
The 'Hitman' moved into coaching after retiring in 2012 and Hedges spent time working under Hatton and had him in his corner when he won the English cruiserweight title in May 2025.
Essex's Hedges, 24, was booed during the weigh-in at Manchester's New Century Hall, with the majority of those in attendance showing support for local fighter Brown.
But Hedges, who pointed to the images of Hatton on his T-shirt, insisted he was unfazed by the reaction.

articles.title: ‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football culture
articles.summary: Head coach says he must accept lack of control in games. ‘Deep down, English players … they go for it’ Thomas Tuchel has admitted there are times when he craves greater control in matches.
body: Tuchel described his team as “maybe not the most economical to play football” in terms of their habit of constantly playing at full throttle. They lost to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in July when they had nothing left in the tank and watched the game slip away after going 1-0 up in the 55th minute. England barely touched the ball thereafter, had no control and were reeled in, Argentina winning with two late goals.

Tuchel said he would like it if his team “became for 10 minutes more like Spain” when the pressure was on – a reference to the ability of the world champions to dominate the ball; their comfort on it. Ultimately, though, Tuchel will always play to the strengths of his players, what they are used to, what they have grown up with – even what the fans in England most like.

It may be an internal battle for him because he is a coach who finds a lack of control “hard to digest”. But as Tuchel looked ahead to the next international cycle and the Nations League games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and Croatia (away), he talked of how he wanted to “embrace the chaos”.

articles.title: Uefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associations
articles.summary: Payout of at least $10m to each association proposed. Leaders want plan to be considered by Fifa Council. The presidents of Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino requesting that Fifa release money from its $6bn (£4.5bn) reserves to its member associations, stating that the plan to fund…
body: Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani proposed a payout of at least $10m to each of Fifa’s 211 member associations (MAs), initially as a one-off during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle. They called for an independent review of Fifa’s financial position and said their own study “raises an important question as to whether the proposed transaction was necessary to deliver greater resources to the MAs”.

The proposed $10m would be handed out on top of money committed by Fifa’s existing Fifa Forward programme, which paid each MA about $8m over the previous four-year cycle. In a separate letter to the presidents of the Asian Football Confederation, the Confederation of African Football, Conmebol (the South American federation) and Oceania, Ceferin and Montagliani asked their counterparts to support the motion. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the AFC president, is expected to send an endorsement of their plan.

The leaders intend their proposal to be considered at the next Fifa Council meeting on 15 October, where Infantino is due to face Fifa’s nominal decision-making body for the first time since scandal engulfed his reign.

articles.title: Carse assault investigation dropped by police
articles.summary: England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no further police action after an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby last month is dropped.
body: England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no further action from the police after an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby last month was dropped.
Footage of Carse appeared on social media, showing him in handcuffs and surrounded by police on Sunday, 23 August. The footage was captured in the early hours of that day.
It emerged that the 31-year-old had been arrested and then de-arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly.
Later that week, after Carse had been removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan, Derbyshire Police confirmed it was looking at allegations of assault.

articles.title: Senegal job an 'absolute dream' for new boss Vieira
articles.summary: Former France international Patrick Vieira, a World Cup winner in 1998, says taking charge of Senegal, the nation of his birth, is an "honour".
body: Patrick Vieira says it is "an honour" to become Senegal head coach, with the decision to take the job "one from the heart".
The 50-year-old was born in the West African nation but subsequently represented France as a player, winning the 1998 World Cup and the 2000 European Championship with Les Bleus.

The former Arsenal midfielder spoke of his "immense pride" to begin his first international job, following stints with New York City, Nice, Crystal Palace, Strasbourg and Genoa, at his unveiling by the Teranga Lions on Friday.
"Being head coach of the Senegal national team is an absolute dream," he told a news conference in Dakar.

articles.title: Leics 'spurred on' by points penalty - Thomas
articles.summary: The 27-point deduction that has the Foxes on the brink of County Championship relegation is fuelling their fight for survival, says head coach Alfonso Thomas.
body: The 27-point deduction that has Leicestershire on the brink of County Championship relegation is what is fuelling their fight for survival, says Foxes head coach Alfonso Thomas.

It was at lunch on the second day of their Division One match against Hampshire this week that Thomas told his Leicestershire players of the impending punishment for the club's breach of pitch regulations in their victory over Glamorgan in August.
After the close of play at Grace Road that same evening, the points were docked and Leicestershire were sent to the bottom of the table.
It meant they needed to beat their relegation rivals to avoid making an immediate return to Division Two.

articles.title: York Valkyrie win at Leeds to book Women's Super League Grand Final vs Wigan
articles.summary: York Valkyrie are through to the 2026 Women's Super League Grand Final against Wigan Warriors following a superb 12-0 semi-final away victory over Leeds Rhinos.
body: York will now face defending champions Wigan in the Grand Final at the Brick Community Stadium on Sunday September 27 (5.30pm kick-off), live on Sky Sports.

York, who were beaten 38-16 by Leeds on August 8, and 44-0 by Wigan a week later on August 15, have totally turned fortunes around since, defeating Leeds at home, St Helens away and Wigan at home before sealing semi-final success.

The opening 21 minutes proved scoreless at Headingley in a tight contest, before York's Liv Wood twisted, turned and wrestled over to ground the ball for a try in the 22nd minute. Tara Jane Stanley converted for the full haul.

As the first half drew to a close and with Leeds camped on the York try-line on the verge of a try, a grubber-kick on the last by Leeds' Ruby Walker proved a poor one and allowed Stanley to gather and run clear.

articles.title: 2. Bundesliga: Fürth and Magdeburg share the spoils in Friday night encounter
articles.summary: It was not quite the nine-goal thriller we have become accustomed to seeing between these sides, though an energetic opening saw Emmanuel Iyoha and Omar Sillah score a goal apiece.
body: Magdeburg got off to the perfect start just five minutes in through Iyoha. A long ball down the right was flicked on by Herbert Bockhorn into the area and into the path of Iyoha, allowing the forward to strike a half-volley past Florian Hellstern at his near post to net his fourth goal of the campaign.
It was the third goal Fürth had conceded inside the opening 15 minutes this season, though they produced a response of their own 20 minutes in.

After starting the move with a short passage of play around the edge of the area, Sillah continued his run into the box before latching onto a Felix Klaus pass and slotting the ball past the onrushing Dominik Reimann to make it 1-1. The goal was awarded following a VAR check after initially being ruled out for offside.
The attacking intent from both sides settled somewhat following an energetic opening 20 minutes, though two good chances arrived in quick succession in the 38th and 39th minutes.

articles.title: No charges against Carse after police close alleged assault investigation
articles.summary: Brydon Carse will not face any charges after Derbyshire Police closed their investigation into an alleged assault following an incident involving the England cricketer at a nightclub in Derby.
body: Last month, Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series against Pakistan.

The 31-year-old was celebrating with Durham players after their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship and was also seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background.
In a statement, Derbyshire Police said: "An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

"Officers attended Molly Malones in the Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday 23 August. A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers."

articles.title: Gerard surges to take clubhouse lead, as McIlroy impresses at Wentworth
articles.summary: Ryan Gerard leapfrogged Adam Scott and Filippo Celli to take a two-shot lead at the halfway stage of the BMW PGA Championship, as Rory McIlroy impressed on day two to finish four shots off the lead.
body: Scott and Celli had climbed to take a share of the clubhouse lead midway through the second round at 10 under par, but Gerard surged in the afternoon, posting a flawless bogey-free seven-under 65 to finish his day at 12 under.

Aaron Rai, who co-led coming into Friday's round, finished tied with Manuel Elvira for fourth, while his playing partners, McIlroy and Ryan Fox, trailed them by one shot, sharing sixth place with five other players at eight under par.
Some big names missed the cut on Friday at Wentworth, including European Ryder Cup stars Jon Rahm and Tommy Fleetwood, who finished at three over on day two.
The Spaniard endured a torrid two days at Wentworth, going 11 over par through 36 holes, to plummet to the worst 36-hole score of his career, and to last place on the leaderboard.
